But the hireling, who is not a shepherd, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters them; because he is a hireling and does not care for the sheep.” And he adds: “For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life for the sheep.” To him be glory forever. Amen.

On the order of the clergy. It follows that the priests should become imitators of their high priest, as he too is of Christ the high priest, in all things: in goodness, compassion, like-mindedness, gentleness, humility, brotherly love, love of the poor, hospitality, and sympathy toward all; being merciful, turning back those who have strayed, visiting all who are sick, not neglecting widows and orphans or the poor, always taking thought for what is good in the sight of God and of men, abstaining from all anger and partiality, from unjust judgment and from love of money; not quick to believe anything against anyone, not severe in judgment, knowing that we are all debtors because of sin. If, then, we ask Christ to forgive us, we too ought to forgive, for we stand before the eyes of the Lord. Likewise the deacons must be blameless before his righteousness, as servants of God and of Christ and not of men. Let them serve diligently, so that they may escape the prophet’s curse and not become liable through negligence. And do not act rashly in anything, as though for the sake of piety, but let all things be done decently and in order, as the Apostle says. Otherwise, what wrong did Uzziah do in burning incense to God? What wrong did Saul do in offering sacrifice? What wrong did the tyrants and the demons do when they spoke truly of God concerning the Lord [?]? Yet their theology was rejected. Let each one remain in the rank of his own ministry.

[?] And the Law too says: “The high priest shall enter the Holy of Holies, and that once a year.” And this in all hierarchical purity: the priests cover the holy things, and “the Levites shall not touch the holy things, lest they die.” And the Lord was angered in wrath at the rashness of Uzziah; and Miriam is struck with leprosy for attempting to lay down laws for the lawgiver. And the man with the demon leapt upon the sons of Sceva. And: “I did not send them, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.” And: “The ungodly man who sacrifices a calf to me is like one who kills a dog.” In short, the perfect justice of God does not tolerate stepping out of rank. And when they say, “In your name we did many mighty works,” he answers, “I do not know you; depart from me, all you workers of lawlessness.” So then, the sacred oracles say, it is not lawful to pursue even just things except in accordance with one’s rank. Each one must attend to himself and not ponder things higher and deeper, but consider only what has been assigned to him according to his rank. And let them be not slanderers, nor double-tongued, but free from the love of money, self-controlled, compassionate toward all, diligent, walking according to the truth of the Lord, who became the servant of all. If we please him in the present age, we shall also receive the age to come, as he promised to raise us from the dead; and if we conduct ourselves worthily of him, we shall also reign with him. For he himself has said: “If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant will be also. If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.” To him be glory forever. Amen.

On reverence for priests. Ignatius the God-bearer writes: “Pay heed to the bishop, so that God may also pay heed to you. I give my life for whoever submits to the bishop, the presbyters and the deacons; may it be mine to have my portion with them in God.” And again: “My witness is he for whom I am in bonds, that I did not learn it from human flesh. But the Spirit was proclaiming, saying this: ‘Do nothing without the bishop.’” We must therefore do nothing without the bishop. For wherever the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as wherever Christ Jesus is named, there the catholic Church is gathered together. For herds of livestock do not go wherever they like, but wherever the shepherds lead them. And those that stray away from the herd

are torn apart by wild beasts, which make the stray their food. It is not permitted without the bishop either to go about [?] or to hold a love feast; but whatever he approves is also pleasing to God. Whoever honors the bishop is honored by God. Whoever does anything behind the bishop’s back serves the devil. It is necessary also to submit to the presbytery [?], as to the apostles of Jesus Christ, our hope. [The deacons must] in every way please everyone. For they are not deacons of food and drink, but servants of the Church of God. They must therefore guard against accusations as against fire. Likewise let all respect the deacons as Jesus Christ, [?] [and the presbyters] as the council of God and the band of the apostles; without these it is not called a Church. The Law also agrees with this teaching, saying: “Take great care to do according to all that the priest tells you [?] … [whoever acts presumptuously] so as not to listen to the priest, that man shall die.” And the prophet Malachi says: “The lips of the priest shall guard knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty. He walked with me in peace, guiding aright, and turned many back from wrongdoing.” And another says: “With all your soul fear the Lord, and revere his priests; with all your strength love the one who made you, and do not forsake his ministers. Fear the Lord and honor the priest.” And again the Law: “The priests shall be holy to their God, for they offer the sacrifices to the Lord their God; and they shall be holy.” And again: “The priest is holy to the Lord God, for he offers the gifts to the Lord our God; and he shall be holy to you.” “And the Lord said to Aaron: I am your portion and inheritance; and Levi shall serve in the tent of witness, and they shall bear the sins of the people. And I have given the offerings to the Levites, because this is their wage, in return for your services.” And Isaiah says: “But you shall be called priests of the Lord, ministers of God.” And Jeremiah: “I will enlarge and fill to overflowing the soul of the [?] …; they shall be clothed with righteousness, and your holy ones shall rejoice.” And Paul says: “For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; they serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, inasmuch as he is the mediator of a better covenant.” And he goes on to say: “We ask you, brothers, to respect those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you, and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.” And

again: “Let the presbyters be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching.” It is fitting, then, beloved friends of God, to revere his priests. For those whom God has made his own and glorified, men too must give what is due to them; and no one takes this honor upon himself, but only the one called by God. It is never lawful, therefore, to oppose a priest; for those who oppose them will incur judgment. “You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.” And the Lord, the great high priest, says: “Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.” “Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward; and whoever receives a righteous man because he is righteous will receive a righteous man’s reward.” To him be glory forever. Amen.

Homily 125. On the expectation of things to come. Whoever looks for the good things to come thrusts away the things of this world, and in his longing for the good things to come passes by everything in this life as a shadow and a cobweb, because of the hope and grace laid up for him. For [the mind?] [?] is naturally there where it has the substance of its possession, that is, where its desire is held captive. Those, therefore, who choose to have their possession in heaven welcome [?] departure from the body. Eagerly awaiting, then, the good things laid up for us, which are beyond compare, let us long for them with all our resolve and with great desire, disregarding the things that do not last, and rejoicing over the eternal and abiding goods, which the human mind cannot grasp. With all vigilance, then, let us guard the heart, awaiting the master of the house, Christ our God, who became poor for our sake and for our salvation took upon himself the sufferings of weakness, so that he might make us sharers in his riches and in the enjoyment of the ineffable glory to come. Let us never cease to love him; and, being [called?] [?] by him, let us enter with him into the dwelling prepared with the Father, and we shall see light in his light. Fearful is the day of his coming, great and exceedingly glorious. Therefore, having these promises, let us rejoice with joy inexpressible and full of glory, always cleansing the soul, lest any root of bitterness spring up and cause trouble, and many be defiled; so that the soul, having come into the purest and [?] light, without spot or wrinkle, may behold that uncreated and blessed nature, where the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are. [?] As the Apostle too says, writing to the Romans: “I appeal to you, therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind,

so that you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect.” And again: “For God has revealed it to us through his Spirit. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God. For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.” And he goes on: “Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given us by God.” And again: “For if the ministry of condemnation had glory, much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory. Indeed, what once had glory has no glory in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it. For if what was passing away came with glory, much more will what remains be in glory.” And elsewhere: “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them; but they are at peace.” And: “Their hope is full of immortality. Having been disciplined a little, they will receive great good, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself, and accepted them as a whole burnt offering; and in the time of his visitation they will shine forth.” And David: “Weeping may lodge for the evening, but joy comes in the morning.” And: “He set my feet in a broad place.” And again the Apostle: “If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of the Father. Set your minds on things above, not on things on earth.” And again: “But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, you have your fruit, which leads to sanctification, and its end, eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” And the Lord says: “Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning, and be like men waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.” And he goes on: “Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and he will come and serve them.” To him be glory forever.

On the calling of God. Since our Lord and God calls us through the Law and the prophets, through the apostles and evangelists, or rather even pleads with us, it is not right for us, out of sloth and slackness, to despise his commandment and neglect our own salvation, lest through our slowness we be shut out of the bridal chamber and deprived of the longed-for bridegroom; and

[?] …lest, after knocking many times, we stay empty-handed and groan in vain. Rather, brothers, let us [?] be earnest, so that we may reach the citadel, or rather our mother city, the Jerusalem above, which is the mother of us all, the land of the living. There the light of life shines out: the unquenchable [?lamp], the sleepless eye, the giver of eternal good things. If then, beloved, we approach our [?] with [?], with longing and with [?], there we shall see every order of [?angels] and archangels and powers and [?], and the good things kept from eternity for his saints. For all who have become lovers of [?] Jerusalem will nurse from her and be nourished at the breasts of her consolation, and from the [?] of her glory. So let us [?cleave] to him who said, “Draw near to me, and I will draw near to you.” Let us yield to the Lawgiver who says, “If you [?listen to] my voice, you will be my own special people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation; you will be sanctified and be holy to me, for I am the Lord your God.” And, “I have [?chosen] you for myself as a special people above all the nations.” And Wisdom says, “Come to me, you who [?desire] me, and be filled with my fruits. For the memory of me is sweeter than honey. Those who eat me will hunger for more, and those who drink me will thirst for more. Whoever obeys me will never be put to shame.” And again: “Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine I have mixed for you; leave folly behind, and you will live.” And David says: “Come to him and be enlightened, and your faces will never be put to shame.” And the Apostle says: “If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.” And he adds: “So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household.” “Let us then approach the throne of grace with [?confidence], so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in time of need.” Our Savior and Lord, who loves humankind, calls us, saying: “Come to me, all you who labor and [?are heavy laden], and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.” And: “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men.” To him be [?] and glory forever. Amen.

On the Fear of God. Whoever truly has the fear of God comes easily to perfect love of God and becomes a disciple and friend of Christ. “For you,” he says, “have loved me.” Such a person clothes himself with purity in this respect. He has renounced the cares of the world, its deceits and pleasures, its carousing and drunkenness, the confusions of Babylon and all the business of this life. He has said farewell to the world and to its nets, entanglements and snares, and while he walks on earth he has chosen to have his citizenship in heaven. Reaching for better things, he said farewell to the world so that he might live a divine, heavenly, angelic life in pure, undefiled and holy worship, serving God the Almighty in the Spirit of God, for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. For its sake he also laid aside the cares of the world. “Fear the Lord,” it says, “and keep his commandments.” If you keep God's commandments, you will be strong in every action, and nothing will compare with what you do. For if you fear the Lord, you will do everything well. This is the fear you must have, and you will be saved. But do not fear the devil. If you fear the Lord, you will master the devil, because there is no power in him. Where there is no power, there is no fear either. But where there is glorious power, there is fear as well. For everyone who has power is also feared, while one who has no power is despised by all. But fear the works of the devil, because they are evil. If you fear the Lord, you will not fear the works of the devil, and you will not do them; instead you will flee from them. So there are two kinds of fear. If you do not want to do evil, fear the Lord, and you will not do it. And if you want to do good, fear the Lord, and you will do it. So the fear of the Lord is stronger, and it is glorious. All who fear him and keep his commandments will live to God. For all creation fears him, but it does not keep his commandments. Only those who fear him and keep his commandments have their life with God. The fear of God compels us to fight against wickedness, and while we fight, the grace of the Lord destroys it. But no one can come into the fear of the Lord unless he is free of all worldly cares, as has been said. When the mind is at rest and free of cares, the fear of God stirs it and carries it into a great love of God's goodness. For those who struggle, fear brings a kind of purification. “The fear of the Lord,” it says, “is pure, enduring for ever and ever.” The fear of the Lord is the begetter of wisdom. Whoever reveres the One will not be afraid of the many. Rather, because of the One, the many will fear him. “For if,” it says, “you fear the Lord your God and listen

to his voice, no one will stand against you to your face, and dread of you will fall on all the nations.” And again he commands: “You shall fear the Lord your God and cleave to him.” And again: “Who will give them such a heart that this people will fear all my commandments, so that it may go well with them?” That is what the Law says. And the prophet Micah says: “For you who fear the Lord the Sun of righteousness will rise, and you will go out and leap like calves set free from their bonds.” And the author of Proverbs says: “The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and a stronghold for the holy; [?] of the Lord is a fountain of life, and it turns a person away from the snare of death.” And again: “Blessed is he to whom the fear of the Lord has been given. The fear of the Lord is life for a man. The fear of the Lord will gladden the heart and give gladness and joy. The fear of the Lord is a gift from the Lord. It will go well in the end with the one who fears the Lord, and in the days of his death he will be blessed. To fear the Lord is the fullness of wisdom, and she makes them drunk with her fruits.” “If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will supply her to you. Those who fear the Lord will be wary of nothing and will not be afraid, for he is their hope.” And David says: “The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak justice.” “For as high as heaven is above the earth, so great has the Lord made his mercy toward those who fear him.” And: “He will do the will of those who fear him; he will hear their prayer and save them.” And: “The Lord is the strength of those who fear him, and his covenant will make itself known to them. For behold, the eyes of the Lord are on those who fear him.” And of himself: “Let my heart rejoice to fear your name.” And the good Spirit says: “I am a companion of all who fear you and keep your commandments.” And James says: “But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.” And Peter says: “In every nation whoever fears the Lord and does what is right is acceptable to him.” And the Lord says: “Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, fear him who, after killing, has authority to destroy the soul [?and body] in Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.” To him be glory forever. Amen. [Lev. 12:32 [?]; Deut. [?]; [?]; Ps. [?]]

On Love for God. Let our discourse now move on from the fear of the Lord to perfect love [?]. By love I mean a love that cannot be broken, that is not cut off or separated by the many kinds of trial and torment, a love that draws near to God and gives birth to children of God. “For love of the Lord and fear surpass all things for enlightenment.” And “the eyes of the Lord are on those who love him.” Whoever loves God with a heart that truly perceives him is known by him. Whoever has gained perfect love for God is present in this life as though he were not present. He considers himself a stranger to the things that are seen, and holds fast to the things that are unseen. He has been wholly transformed into the love of God, as one who has gone out of love for himself through the love of God. “For if we are beside ourselves,” he says, “it is for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for you.” Whoever loves himself cannot love God. But whoever [?does not spare] himself for the sake of the surpassing wealth of God's love, that person loves God. The Law declares it first, saying: “I am the Lord, who shows mercy to those who love me and keep my ordinances.” And another says: “A secure seed are those who fear the Lord.” And: “An honored plant are those who love him.” And: “A man's mercy is for his neighbor, but the Lord's mercy is for all flesh; he lifts up and enlightens the eyes.” And Wisdom says: “I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find knowledge. Wealth and glory are mine. It is better to gain me than gold and precious stone.” And David, out of his warm love for God, cried out continually: “O God, my God, I rise early to seek you; my soul has thirsted for you. In how many ways my flesh longs for you, in a desert land, trackless and waterless!” And again: “I will love you, O Lord, my strength. The Lord is my firm foundation, my refuge and my [?deliverer].” And: “Lord, all my desire is before you, and my groaning is not hidden from you.” And again: “My soul has thirsted for God, the mighty, the living. When shall I come and appear before the face of God?” And: “My soul has longed to desire your judgments at all

times, for your [?words] are sweet to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth.” “Eat honey, my son,” it says, “for the honeycomb is good, so that your throat may be sweetened. In the same way perception and wisdom will come to your soul.” And John says: “Beloved, God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God in him.” And he goes on: “Not that we loved him, but that he loved us and sent his Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.” And Paul says: “But in all these things we are more than conquerors through God who loved us.” And he adds: “For those who love God, all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.” And [?again]: “Who will separate us from the love of God? Will affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?” And he goes on: “For I am convinced that neither death nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” And the Lord says: “Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and reveal myself to him.” [?You see] that love for God brings his self-revelation and makes us able to receive him. Whoever sincerely loves God regards himself as a stranger and sojourner in this life, and such a person has undergone the good transformation. Those who meditate unceasingly on the holy name of Christ in the depths of their hearts can one day see his light as well. For when the mind holds on to it with close attention, it burns away all the filth of the soul, and one perceives this keenly. “For our God is a consuming fire,” it says. This is why the Lord calls the soul to a great love of his own glory. Nothing kindles the heart and moves it to the love of God as much as theology, that is, contemplation of God. It brings forth all that belongs to his grace. Before everything else it grants gifts to the soul of the one who loves God, and sows in his heart tears as sweet as honey. For with his soul and its ruling faculty he continually beholds him through longing. A soul that rejoices in the love of God will not be afraid, when the time comes for it to leave the body, of the ruler of this air or of the powers of darkness. Instead, out of its love for God, [?rejoicing] it flies with the angels of peace, as if from a foreign land to its own home. “For I have the desire,” he says, “to depart and be with Christ.” The soul that has love, which is the fulfillment of the law, will be caught up in the clouds at the Lord's coming to meet him. We almost forgot the [?love] of the bride, the Church, in the Song of Songs for the Bridegroom, Christ. What a loss that would have been! For she says: “Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for

your breasts are better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfumes is better than all spices. Your name is perfume poured out. That is why the maidens have loved you. They have [?drawn] you; we will run after you toward the fragrance of your perfume. Let us rejoice and be glad in you; uprightness has loved you.” And again: “Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture your flock, where do you rest at noon? For see, you are fair, and [?lovely] too. I longed for your shade and sat in it, and your fruit was sweet to my throat.” And urging others on, she says: “I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.” And again: “Show me your face, and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your [?face] is lovely.” Moses was like this when he cried out, “Show me your face, so that I may see you and know you.” And again: “I sought him whom my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go, for I am wounded with love. For love is strong as death; many waters cannot quench love.” Such was the soul of Peter, who said, “Lord, where are you going?” and, “To whom shall we go?” The Lord asked him a third time, “Peter, do you love me?” And he said, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” And again the Lord says to his disciples: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.” To him be glory forever. Amen.

On Adoption. Glory to your goodness, O Master who loves humankind, who loves the poor, tender-hearted, [?], lover of good, Lord who bears no grudge! We once scorned your commandment in paradise and were made dead by sin and by our own will, yet you not only set us free but also proclaimed us your own children. And until now we have lived carelessly where your commandments are concerned, so that in us is fulfilled the saying, “I have begotten sons and raised them up, but they have rejected me.” Who could ever recount the ocean of your compassion, O patient guardian of our souls, God Almighty, and Lord of your mercy? For you said through your prophet Hosea: “I will call Not-My-People ‘My People,’ and Not-Beloved ‘Beloved’; and in the place where it was said, ‘You are [?not] my people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.” And John says: “Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we shall be has not yet been revealed. But we know that when he is revealed we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.” And Paul says: “And all of us, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, [Song 1:3; ibid. 7; [?]]

are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Lord, the Spirit.” And again: “In love he predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ, for himself. Be imitators of God, then, as his beloved children, and walk in love, just as Christ loved us.” And again: “And not only creation, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait for adoption, the redemption of our bodies.” And again: “And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, ‘Abba, Father.’ So you are no longer a slave but a son; and if a son, then also an heir of God through Jesus Christ.” And again: “For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that leads back into fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, ‘Abba, Father.’ The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God; and if children, then heirs: heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ.” And the fellow heirs of Christ “will be called sons of the Most High.” When they see the kingdom of God in glory, the gates of the kingdom will be opened to them there, and they will enter the Father's treasuries. God will show them his saints from all the ages, the Sun of righteousness will appear to them, “and they will go out and leap like calves set free from their bonds.” “And he will transform our lowly body so that it is conformed to his own glorious body.” There “youth will be renewed like the eagle's” [?], and they will see the land of promise, and “they will be comforted on her knees, as one whom a mother comforts.” So the Lord will make righteousness and gladness spring up before all who love him with a sincere heart. And we too, beloved, should revere the one who has honored us so greatly and raised us to such a height. “Let us serve him in fear,” as our Master by nature, “and rejoice in him with trembling,” as our Father by grace, “lest the Lord be angry” and we fall away from so great an adoption. Whoever falls away from it becomes like Judas the traitor, a son of perdition, of Gehenna and of the devil. But may we never depart from the love of our Savior and God, Jesus Christ. For he gave us authority “to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy.” “To as many of us as received him he gave authority to become children of God.” And he said, “Do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.” To him be glory forever. [John 1:12; Phil. 3:21 [?]]

On the Kingdom of Heaven. Now that we have kept the commandments of God described above, let us go up to the kingdom of heaven. The struggle for it is great, and the rest it brings is infinitely greater. Think of someone who longs for an earthly kingdom. He shows great valor in wars and dangers, in sleepless nights, cares and toils, and he counts as nothing all the hardships that come upon him, in the hope of the kingdom he dreams of, though it is temporary and has no substance. And sometimes, after he has endured every toil and thinks he already holds what he hoped for in his hands, someone nobody suspected wears the crown in his place. If that is so, what struggles must be endured by the one who wants to reign with Christ forever, with no one to succeed him! What zeal and eagerness he needs, what sleepless nights, cares and dangers, what hardships and trials, both hidden and open, what tortures and deaths! That is why the saints who went before us, men and women and children, struggled even to death to gain the kingdom of heaven. For the kingdom of heaven is taken by force, and those who force themselves in everything seize it. Whoever has truly made himself a eunuch for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, or has remained a virgin, is bound in every way to show himself worthy of the kingdom. For the kingdom of heaven is not gained by words, or by outward dress, or by a name, or by birth, or by looks, or by strength, or by age. It is gained by the power of faith, a faith that shows itself in works of faith. For the righteous person will proclaim his faith by showing it actively. And what does “actively” mean, if not by putting the commandments of Christ into practice? It also means keeping away from their opposites, that is, from fleshly, or rather diabolical, ways of thinking. These are: fornication, impurity, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of rage, selfish ambition, slander, dissension, envy, murder, drunkenness, carousing, coarse jesting, foolish talk, laughter, folly, mockery, whispering, bitterness, anger, shouting, blasphemy, idle chatter, malice, the invention of evil, perjury, talking too much, twisted speech, empty babbling, causing trouble [?], vulgarity, constant wrangling, lawsuits, stupidity, conceit, and pride in one's family, looks, country, wealth, physical courage or eloquence. They also include rivalry combined with love of quarreling, hatred, bearing grudges, a quick temper, lasting resentment, deceit, revenge, gluttony, insatiability, and greed, which is idolatry. Then come love of money, which is the root of all evils, love of the world, vainglory, love of power, self-will, rashness, and boastfulness, which is called a plague [?]. Last comes arrogance, which God opposes. Whoever has these things, and others like them, in himself is fleshly and a son of the adversary. For what is born of the flesh is flesh. Whoever is of the earth speaks of earthly things, because his mind is set on earthly works. For the mind of the flesh is hostile to God. It does not submit to God's law; indeed it cannot. And in such a person the Spirit of God does not dwell. “For my Spirit,” he says, “shall not remain in human beings

…to these forever, because they are flesh. “If anyone, then, does not have the Spirit of God, he does not belong to him.” For whoever has the Spirit of God walks by the Spirit of God, and by the Spirit of God puts to death the deeds of the body, and lives to God, pummeling the flesh and bringing it into subjection, so that the holy and peaceable Spirit may dwell in him. And, guarded by the Spirit, he will bear the fruit of faith, virtue, wisdom, purity, self-control, love, kindness, endurance, hope, concord, temperance, praise and sanctification. These things, and things like them, lead into the kingdom of heaven; but all the things mentioned before, the thoughts of the flesh, do not come near the kingdom of heaven. But before I bring to a close this discourse on the kingdom of heaven, it seems necessary to me to make known to you, honored Father Eustathius, a thought that has occurred to me just now. It is perhaps itself useful, as is likely, for the discourse on the kingdom; or rather, as it seems to me at least, it is more beneficial and profitable than anything else. Our iniquities have multiplied and risen above our heads. We were not disciplined by the Chaldean scourge, nor did their yoke tame our stiff necks, but we grow still bolder in evil. For this reason, by God's permission, Satan has brought upon us a blow that can reach the entrails, the marrow and the bones. We have heard that someone has come in the East, a forerunner of the Antichrist, who wishes to seize the throne of Antioch. He is called Athanasius, or rather “deathless death,” and he preaches the doctrines of Apollinaris, Eutyches, Severus and Jacob. This report has greatly troubled the orthodox inhabitants of the holy city and the monasteries around it. As I have written to you, you must of necessity travel through many countries, places and islands, and it happens that there are many heresies in various places. So that you may not fall in with any of them through ignorance, I have set down for you all the heresies from the coming of Christ until now, so that you and those with you may guard yourselves against them as against snakes. But this is not the occasion to say what each heresy believes. Let this be a short and sure sign to keep you safe: all heresies that are named after a human being, such as the Arians, the Nestorians, the Severians and others like them, are heresies of the devil. For the Catholic Church has not been called by a human name; instead we are all called Christians, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. “For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved,” except the Lord Jesus Christ alone, to the glory of God the Father, with the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.

At the beginning of the book we have set out sufficiently the faith, that is, the consubstantiality of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. But now, because of the heresy that has arisen, we openly confess and proclaim this. Our Lord Jesus Christ is the only-begotten Son and Word of the Father, light from light, true God from true God. He was incarnate and became man by the Holy Spirit and from the holy and glorious Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary. He is perfect God and also perfect man, one and only Son, both before the incarnation and after the incarnation. He is consubstantial with the Father according to the divinity and consubstantial with us according to the humanity, having become man like us in all things except sin. He was begotten of the Father before the ages according to the divinity, and in the last days the same one was born, for us and for our salvation, of the holy Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary. He is one and only Son, made known in two natures without confusion, without change and without division. For two natures came together with one another in a union that cannot be torn apart or separated, without confusion and without change. The flesh is flesh and not divinity, even though it became the flesh of God. Likewise the Word is God and not flesh, even though by the divine economy he made the flesh his own. We say, therefore, that there are two natures, but one Christ and Son and Lord, the Word of God, who became man and was made flesh. For the natures brought together into true unity are different, but out of both there is one Christ and Son. This is not because the difference of the natures was abolished by the union. Rather, divinity and humanity, through their inexpressible and incomprehensible coming together into unity, brought about for us the Lord and Christ and Son. This is what we, that is, the Catholic Church, believe, as did the great luminaries and teachers of the truth, Athanasius, Basil, Gregory, John, and Cyril of the great city of Alexandria. Those who do not think so we turn away from and anathematize, together with the heresies listed below, which sprang up at various times after the coming of the Lord. Their names are these: Simonians, Menandrians, Saturnilians, Basilidians, Nicolaitans, Gnostics, Carpocratians, Cerinthians, Nazoraeans, Ebionites, Valentinians, Secundians, Ptolemaeans, Marcosians, Colorbasians, Heracleonites, Ophites, Cainites, Sethians, Archontics, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Lucianists, Apellians, Severians, Tatianists, Encratites, the Cataphrygians, with the Montanists and Ascodrugites, the Pepuzians, also called Priscillianists or Quintillianists, with whom are joined the Artotyrites, the Quartodecimans, the Alogi,

the Adamians, the Sampsaeans, also called Elkesaites, [?] … Meletians, Arians, also called Ariomanites, Audians, Photinians, Marcellians, Semi-Arians, Pneumatomachi, Aerians, Aetians, also called Anomoeans, Eunomians, Eudoxians, Dimoerites, also called Apollinarians, Antidicomarianites, those who make cakes in the name of that same Mary, and Messalians, also called Euchites. Holy Epiphanius set them out up to this point. After these came Evagrius and Didymus, who held Origen's views on preexistence and restoration; Theodore of Mopsuestia, Diodore and Nestorius, who were of one mind in speaking of two sons; Maris the Persian, who agrees with them; and the so-called Letter [?of Ibas]. After these came Eutyches, who held to phantasm, mere appearance and confusion. He was followed by Dioscorus, Theodosius, Gaianus, Timothy Aelurus, Peter, who devised the addition of “who was crucified” to the Trisagion, Peter Mongus, Severus the Acephalus, Soterichus from Samaria [?] in Cappadocia, Philoxenus of Hierapolis, Amphilochius the Pisidian, Jacob the Syrian, Julian, and anyone else like them. I have sent you these things, honored Father Eustathius, to show you that each heresy, being named after some human being, teaches apostasy from Christ. For they do not bear to be called Christians, but Nestorians, Severians, Jacobites, or some other name from those written above. But let us now come to our senses again from the [?] … “made war with the saints and prevailed against them, until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the saints of the Most High; and the time came, and the saints took possession of the kingdom. And the kingdom and the authority and the greatness of the kings under the whole of heaven were given to the saints of the Most High.” And John says: “This is the promise that he promised to give us: eternal life.” And Paul says: “Our citizenship is in heaven, and from it we also await a Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory.” And again: “He rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love.” “Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us have grace, through which we may serve God acceptably.” “For we know that if our earthly house, this tent, is destroyed, we have a

building from God, a house not made with hands, in the heavens.” And Peter says: “For in this way entry into the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to us.” And our Lord and Savior says: “The kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.” And: “The kingdom of heaven is within you.” And again: “Blessed are the poor in spirit.” And: “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” And: “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you.” “For the Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness, and throw them into the furnace of fire. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.” For his is the kingdom and the power and the glory, of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, always, now and ever, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

ON PRAYER AND CONFESSION. O Lord God almighty, great and wonderful, you keep your covenant and your mercy for those who love you and keep your commandments. Remember your compassion and your mercies, for they are from of old. Do not forget your covenant, in which you said: “If you do not keep my commandments, I will punish your iniquities with the rod and your wrongdoings with scourges; but I will not take my mercy away from you, and I will not set aside what has gone out from my lips.” Let your words be confirmed, good Master, and take away our sins, you who are compassionate and long-suffering. For righteousness belongs to you, the Lord our God, but shame has covered our faces, as it does this day. For we have sinned before you, Lord, and have not listened to your voice and walked in the ordinances you set before us. We have rejected you, Lord our God, and these great evils have clung to us. And

[col.] 1851 ANTIOCHUS. Even so we did not turn back to keep your ordinances. Instead each of us follows his own evil mind and does evil before your eyes. And see, our holy places are desolate, the city is burned with fire, and the people are captive. We have become a reproach to those around us, a place they shun. We have been brought low and not raised high, because we sinned against you, the Lord our God, and did not listen to your voice. Therefore you have cast us off and torn us down; you have shaken the earth and thrown it into turmoil. But since you are long-suffering and rich in mercy, heal its breaches, for it has been shaken violently. For your people, who are called by your new name, have seen hard things. The words of your prophets have been fulfilled upon us: “The nations have come into your inheritance and defiled your holy temple,” in which the mystery of the economy of your only-begotten Son was accomplished, “and they have set your sanctuary on fire.” “They have made Jerusalem like a watchman's hut in an orchard,” “and the corpses of your servants” lie in the midst of Jerusalem and all around it, “and there was no one to bury them.” Our strength, our beauty and our salvation, the cross of your Christ, you have handed over to our adversaries. We have become a reproach to our neighbors, and a scorn and a mockery to those far off and to all the nations, because you have turned us back before our enemies. Those who hate us plundered us for themselves. You gave us up like sheep to be eaten and scattered us among the nations. You sold your people for nothing, and there was no great price in the shouts over us. You handed us over to lawless enemies and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the earth. Yet in all these scourges we did not [?], because our mind is earnestly set on evil from our youth, and we grow ever bolder in evil. Truly you alone are just, Lord, in all that you have done to us. For we know that our sins have stood up against us, and our iniquities before you are very many, Lord. But let your mercy, Lord, come to us quickly, for you are among us, Lord, and your holy name has been called upon us. Let the wrath of your anger subside, and do not put us to shame forever. Do not remember our iniquities, whether old or recent, and do not judge us unworthy of your [?]. But remember that you redeemed us with your precious blood. We have sinned: be merciful, Lord. We have done wrong: forgive, Master. We have offended you: be reconciled. Let your face shine, Lord, upon your servants in captivity, and send forth help from yourself, Mighty One, and [deliver]

your people from all distress. Redeem them from all lawlessness and from the hand of the lawless. Scatter every danger, Master, in your compassion. Do not hand over your inheritance to destruction forever because of our iniquities, but let your compassion, Lord our God, come quickly to meet us, for your mercies have been upon your creation from of old. You have become the refuge of us all and the salvation of those who hope in you. Be a tower of strength for us, Lord, against our enemies, and do not let souls who confess you perish at the hands of those who do not know you. Do not allow your inheritance, Lord, to be dishonored by a shameless nation. Instead, Lord, incline your ear and hear. Look down from your holy heaven upon our devastation and that of your city Jerusalem, which is called by your name, and upon your Church, which you built upon the rock, saying, “The gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” Hear, Lord, the prayer of your servants, and give ear to our supplication, and let your face shine upon your sanctuary. For we bring our plea to you trusting not in our own righteous deeds (since we are always provoking you), but in your great compassion, Lord. Hear, Lord; be merciful, Lord; give heed; spare your people, Master, “and do not give your inheritance over to reproach, for the nations to curse it, so that they do not say, ‘Where is their God?’” Let your name not be blasphemed because of our iniquities among the nations that do not know you. Righteousness belongs to you, Lord our God, but shame of face belongs to us until now. For until now we have not been ashamed, because we are stiff-necked. “If the Ethiopian can change his skin,” then we too can change our most wicked disposition. All these evils have come upon us, and still we were not ashamed and did not repent. Instead we added sin upon sin, and we did not entreat your face, Lord, so that we might turn away from the thoughts of our evil heart. And you kept watch, Lord, over our evil deeds and brought upon us the rod of your anger. For you are just, Lord, in all things, because we did not listen to your voice and walk in your commandments. But now, Lord our God, you who rescued us from the error of idols with signs and wonders and have made a name for yourself to this day, relent, Lord. For we are left few upon the earth, and we have all become like the unclean. Our righteousness is like a filthy rag, and because of our sins we have withered and fallen like leaves. And now, Lord, you are our Father, and we are clay, all of us the work of your hands. Do not be exceedingly angry with us, and do not remember our sins in due time. But look upon us, Lord, for we are all your people. Your holy city has become a wilderness, the glory of Zion has been burned with fire, and all our glorious things

have fallen. Yet in all these things you held back, Lord, and humbled us greatly, because we did not walk in the good way but followed after our sins. But spare your people, Lord, and your inheritance, and deliver us from the hand of our enemies for your name's sake, so that all [?] may know that you, Lord our God, are mighty in war, and that your compassion, from generation to generation, reaches a people in despair. But what shall we sinners pray, O Master, lover of mankind? We do not know how we ought to pray, for we are earth and ashes. Yet we have an Advocate on our behalf before your goodness: your spotless Word. Through the [?] of your mercy you sent him to call back his own creature, and he was made flesh and crucified for [us]. He blotted out the bond that stood against us and has become [?] for our sins. And your Holy Spirit also intercedes for us, not as a servant would, but in a manner worthy of God, lovingly caring for your own creature. Remember, O Master, your great goodness toward us and the [?] of your only-begotten Son. Send down upon us your compassion and grace and the gift of your Holy Spirit, so that by his good presence he may guide us to do what is pleasing to you and to attain eternal life. We who are unworthy, Master, therefore ask boldly, because of the one who said it, your timeless Son and Word, O Father, our Lord Jesus Christ: “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.” And again: “If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?” For to you belong all glory, honor and worship, to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and to the ages of [ages].
